document.content:
{
  "title": "Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping — Program kickoff (Reliability Program)",
  "space": "eng-sre",
  "author": "Rafael Mendes",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-11-26",
  "last_updated": "2026-01-08",
  "reviewers": [
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Allison Grant",
    "Ethan Park",
    "Vanessa Ortiz",
    "Sofia Ivanova",
    "Dev Patel",
    "Lauren Bishop"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "reliability",
    "incidents",
    "taxonomy",
    "ownership",
    "sla",
    "oncall",
    "observability"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-taxonomy-v1-definitions.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/incident-ownership-mapping-and-remediation-sla-matrix.json",
    "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/incident-classification-policy.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/incident-taxonomy-dashboards-spec.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0142-incident-taxonomy-as-required-incident-field.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/tying-incident-types-to-slos-and-error-budgets.json"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "## Summary
This page kicks off the Reliability Program initiative “Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping”. The goal is to reduce incident frequency and improve MTTR by standardizing (1) incident classification, (2) owner accountability, and (3) remediation expectations (SLA timers) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private tiers.

We are targeting a taxonomy that is:
- Easy to apply live during an incident (decision-tree friendly)
- Low-cardinality and stable (safe for metric labels and dashboards)
- Aligned with real operational control boundaries (single primary owner per type)
- Useful for reporting, prioritization, and error budget breakdowns

## Why we’re doing this
Current incident labeling is inconsistent (freeform tags, service-only naming, inconsistent ownership), which causes:
- Ambiguity during response (who owns mitigation vs who is consulted)
- Postmortems that are hard to roll up into actionable themes
- Dashboards that can’t reliably show incident drivers by type/team
- SLA tracking that varies by commander judgment and tier

The outcome of this initiative is a v1 taxonomy and ownership map that becomes required in incident tooling and postmortems.

## Objectives (v1)
1) **Standardized incident taxonomy**
   - Define a bounded set of top-level incident types and subtypes.
   - Provide clear definitions, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and examples.
   - Provide a quick decision tree that works under time pressure.

2) **Ownership mapping and escalation**
   - Map each incident type/subtype to **one primary owning team/service**.
   - Define secondary/consulted teams and when to escalate.
   - Ensure mappings match actual “can mitigate now” boundaries.

3) **Remediation SLAs by tier and severity**
   - Define time-to-mitigate (TTM) and time-to-fix (TTF) expectations.
   - Align with customer commitments for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
   - Implement timers and breach notifications in tooling.

4) **Tooling integration and enforcement**
   - incident-bot: required incident_type/subtype + owner resolution.
   - postmortems: required taxonomy fields and outcome reporting.
   - dashboards/alerts: incident volume, MTTA/MTTR, SLA compliance by type/owner.

## Non-goals (v1)
- Creating a deep root-cause taxonomy (root cause lives in postmortems; taxonomy is for consistent classification and reporting).
- Producing a long-term product roadmap unrelated to incident reduction.
- Capturing every edge case on day 1. v1 should be stable; we’ll iterate with v1.1 after adoption.
- Replacing security incident management. This work aligns with security classification, but security incidents remain owned and tracked via Security Ops.

## Scope
### In-scope incident classes
The taxonomy must cover customer-impacting incidents and high-severity internal incidents that threaten reliability. The initial in-scope set:
- **Availability / 5xx / overload** (including saturation and service errors)
- **Latency regressions** (p95/p99 and tail latency spikes)
- **Streaming disconnects / reset spikes**
- **Routing/fallback misbehavior** (wrong policy, wrong fallback target, thrash)
- **Capacity/fleet shortages** (GPU scarcity, provisioning lag, regional constraints)
- **Control plane outages** (config writes/reads, policy evaluation failures)
- **Auth/RBAC failures** (token validation, permission enforcement failures)
- **Telemetry/metrics blind spots** (monitoring gaps, missing signals, alert failures)
- **Private deployment connectivity/config issues** (VPC/on-prem DNS/TLS, network paths, upgrades)

### Out of scope
- Purely informational events with no reliability risk (e.g., benign deploy notices).
- Low-priority bugs that do not threaten SLOs and do not require incident response.

## What “incident type” means in this program
An **incident type** is a stable category used for:
- paging/triage routing (where applicable)
- consistent on-call communication (“what kind of failure is this?”)
- dashboards and reporting (low-cardinality)
- accountability (single primary owner)

An incident type is **not**:
- the full root cause (“kernel bug in driver X”) or a postmortem narrative
- a freeform service name (“router”, “gateway”, “k8s”) without classification intent

## Deliverables
- **Confluence**
  - Taxonomy definitions + decision tree
  - Ownership mapping + remediation SLA matrix
  - Incident classification policy update
  - Postmortem template updates
  - ADR: taxonomy required in incident tooling
- **Engineering work**
  - incident-bot updates (required fields, owner resolution, closure gating)
  - control plane config for owner mapping (versioned, reviewed, auditable)
  - observability changes (metric label allowlist + guardrails)
  - dashboards and breach alerting

## Stakeholders and working group
### Core working group
- **SRE (program lead):** Rafael Mendes
- **Executive sponsor (SRE):** Sean Gallagher
- **SLO/SLA dashboards:** Aisha Bello
- **Observability standards:** Allison Grant
- **Dashboards/alerting implementation:** Sergio Costa
- **Incident data analysis:** Mei Lin
- **Control plane owner mapping:** Ethan Park
- **Routing ownership + escalation:** Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon
- **Fleet/capacity ownership:** Vanessa Ortiz, Harish Reddy
- **Private connectivity/networking:** Victor Alvarez
- **Runtime taxonomy SME:** Sofia Ivanova, Noah Patel
- **Security alignment:** Fiona McCarthy
- **Support/CS escalation mapping:** Dev Patel, Owen Phillips
- **Tier SLA stakeholders:** Nikhil Sharma (Hosted), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Vivek Kulkarni (Private)
- **Tooling integration:** Dylan Brooks, Devon Price
- **Docs/training:** Elliot Price, Kira Thompson
- **Program management:** Talia Benson

### Decision ownership
- Taxonomy definitions: SRE + Observability + Runtime/Routing/Fleet SMEs
- Primary owner mapping: SRE + owning EM/Director of the mapped team
- Remediation SLA targets: SRE + Product/Tier stakeholders + Support/CS
- Tooling enforcement: SRE + incident-bot/tooling owners

## Cadence and timeline
We’ll run this as a 6–10 week program with explicit checkpoints.

### Cadence
- **Weekly working sync (45 min):** SRE + leads from Platform/Routing/Fleet/Runtime/Observability
- **Office hours (30 min):** open Q&A for on-call engineers
- **Two taxonomy workshops (90 min each):** definitions + decision tree convergence
- **Review/signoff window:** async review via Confluence comments + email thread

### Proposed phases
1) **Discovery + data pull** (Week 1–2)
   - Analyze last 90 days incidents + support escalations.
   - Propose top 10–15 categories, identify ambiguous clusters.

2) **Taxonomy workshop(s)** (Week 2–3)
   - Finalize top-level types and the decision tree.
   - Confirm “primary vs contributing” guidance for multi-cause incidents.

3) **Ownership + SLA alignment** (Week 3–5)
   - Validate owners with EMs/Directors.
   - Align remediation SLAs with Hosted/Dedicated/Private expectations.

4) **Tooling integration** (Week 5–8)
   - incident-bot required fields and owner resolution.
   - control plane config and audit.
   - metric label changes and dashboard rollout.
   - SLA timers and breach alerting.

5) **Rollout + training + enforcement** (Week 8–10)
   - On-call playbook updates.
   - Announcement + office hours.
   - Enforce classification (cannot close without type/owner).

## Success metrics
We will track program success using adoption, data quality, and reliability outcomes.

### 1) Classification compliance (adoption)
- **>= 90%** of incidents created via incident-bot have incident_type and owner set within **15 minutes** of incident declaration by end of Week 2 post-rollout.
- **>= 95%** compliance by end of Week 6 post-rollout.
- **< 5%** incidents closed with incident_type = “Unknown/Unclassified” by end of Week 6 post-rollout.

### 2) Reporting coverage (observability)
- Incident dashboards show, at minimum:
  - incident volume by incident_type and primary owner
  - MTTA/MTTR by incident_type
  - remediation SLA breach rate by tier/severity
- **>= 90%** of incidents are represented in dashboards with stable labels (no exploding cardinality).

### 3) Reliability outcomes (program impact)
We expect a lagging improvement once reporting is stable.
- Reduce incidents in top 3 recurring categories by **20% QoQ** (baseline established via 90-day backfill).
- Improve median MTTR by **15%** for incidents in categories with clear ownership and playbooks.
- Reduce “handoff time” (time from incident declare to correct owning team engaged) by **25%**.

## Guardrails and constraints
- **Low-cardinality taxonomy:** prefer ~10–15 top-level types with small subtype sets.
- **Single primary owner:** one accountable team per type/subtype; others listed as secondary/consulted.
- **Metric label allowlist:** taxonomy values must be enumerated; “unknown/unclassified” is an allowed bucket.
- **Tier-aware SLAs:** Dedicated/Private commitments may differ; document carve-outs for cloud-provider force majeure and customer-caused incidents.

## Working assumptions
- The incident commander (IC) sets initial incident_type during declaration and can update it as evidence changes.
- Multi-cause incidents require:
  - one primary incident_type for reporting and SLA policy
  - contributing systems recorded separately in the incident record/postmortem

## Risks and mitigations
- **Risk: Taxonomy is too complex to use live**
  - Mitigation: decision tree first; keep v1 small; add examples for common confusions.

- **Risk: Ownership disputes (Routing vs Fleet vs Runtime vs Platform)**
  - Mitigation: map by “who can mitigate now”, not who wrote the code; document escalation and contributing factors.

- **Risk: Observability label cardinality blow-up**
  - Mitigation: strict allowlist; sampling rules; review by Observability prior to enabling labels broadly.

- **Risk: SLAs set unrealistic expectations**
  - Mitigation: tier stakeholder signoff; explicit carve-outs; pilot timers before hard enforcement.

## Initial decisions (kickoff)
- v1 taxonomy will be **mandatory** in incident tooling for new incidents after rollout.
- Ownership mapping will be stored in a **versioned, reviewed control-plane config** with audit logs.
- We will support “Unknown/Unclassified” temporarily, but will treat it as an adoption defect and track reasons.

## Open questions
- How do we handle incidents that start as “capacity” but are later found to be “routing policy misbehavior”? (Proposed: update incident_type; keep contributing factors recorded.)
- What are the tier-specific SLA carve-outs for region-wide cloud-provider outages? (Needs final alignment with Dedicated/Private stakeholders.)
- What is the appropriate place to store subtype-to-runbook mappings: control plane config vs incident-bot code? (Leaning: control plane config for auditability.)

## How to contribute
- Comment on the taxonomy draft page with:
  - confusing categories and specific incidents that don’t fit
  - suggested examples to add to the decision tree
  - ownership boundary concerns (“who mitigates this at 3am?”)
- Bring disputed mappings to the weekly sync; SRE will drive to an explicit decision with EM/Director signoff.

## Contact and escalation
- Program lead: Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Executive sponsor: Sean Gallagher (SRE)
- For tooling issues (incident-bot): Dylan Brooks / Devon Price
- For observability schema concerns: Allison Grant

---
### Change log
- 2026-01-08: Updated success metrics to include handoff-time target; clarified multi-cause guidance; added initial decisions section.
- 2025-11-26: Initial kickoff page created.",

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024.json",
    "title": "New Hire Orientation & Tooling Playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"New Hire Orientation & Tooling Playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"company-handbook\",\n  \"author\": \"Maya Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"people-ops\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-11-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-02-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Liam Chen\",\n    \"Rupa Singh\",\n    \"Andre Gomez\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"onboarding\",\n    \"new-hire\",\n    \"tools\",\n    \"people-ops\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/company-handbook/00_overview/employee-handbook-2024\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/one-click-dev-setup\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Overview:\\\\n\\\\nThis playbook is the canonical guide for orienting new hires at Redwood Inference. It combines the people-ops onboarding checklist, role-specific 30/60/90 templates, access provisioning procedures, an internal tools primer, and first-week agenda recommendations. Use this doc to coordinate hiring managers, IT, security, and the new hire so that day 1 is productive and secure.\\\\n\\\\nWho this is for:\\\\n- Hiring managers preparing a new joiner\\\\n- People Ops coordinators running orientation\\\\n- IT/Security staff provisioning accounts and devices\\\\n- New hires who want a single source of truth for the first 90 days\\\\n\\\\nGoals:\\\\n- Ensure all essential accounts and hardware are provisioned by day 1 (target SLA below).\\\\n- Provide a clear 30/60/90 learning and success plan for common roles.\\\\n- Standardize tooling orientation so engineers, product, and SREs can ship quickly and securely.\\\\n\\\\nQuick links (internal):\\\\n- People Ops onboarding JIRA: /jira/POPS-ONBOARD\\\\n- Device procurement form: /tools/device-request\\\\n- Okta SSO admin: https://okta.redwood.local\\\\n- Console sandbox: https://console-sandbox.redwood.local\\\\n\\\\nOnboarding SLAs (target):\\\\n| Item | SLA (business days) | Owner |\\\\n|---|---:|---|\\\\n| Okta / core SSO account enabled | 1 | People Ops / IT |\\\\n| GitHub org membership + repo access | 2 | Eng manager / DevOps |\\\\n| PagerDuty & Datadog alert access | 2 | Eng SRE |\\\\n| Laptop procurement (if new) | 3-7 | IT procurement |\\\\n| Security training assigned | 1 | Security |\\\\n| Full access to Redwood Console (prod sandbox role) | 3 | Platform team |\\\\n\\\\nNote: these are targets. Use expedited channel when access will block day-1 work.\\\\n\\\\nDay 0-1 Checklist (numbered steps for managers + Ops):\\\\n1. Confirm start date and arrival window with People Ops.\\\\n2. Add new hire to People Ops onboarding JIRA and attach signed offer.\\\\n3. Create Okta account and add to SSO groups (engineering/product/sales as appropriate).\\\\n4. Request laptop via Device procurement form (include preferred OS, accessories).\\\\n5. Add to relevant Slack channels, Mail Groups, and Confluence spaces.\\\\n6. Grant GitHub org membership and base repo access (create PR template if repo requires).\\\\n7. Assign mandatory trainings: security, privacy, code of conduct (links provided in the People Ops JIRA).\\\\n8. Schedule 60-minute orientation with People Ops and 30-minute manager check-in for day 1.\\\\n9. Assign onboarding buddy and create calendar invites for first-week paired sessions.\\\\n10. Run through initial access verification script (see Access Verification below).\\\\n\\\\nAccess Verification (run with new hire on day 1):\\\\n- Okta SSO login successful\\\\n- Email access and distribution lists verified\\\\n- Slack signed in on desktop and mobile\\\\n- GitHub access to at least 2 repos: onboarding and team repo\\\\n- Console sandbox access: able to view the \\u2018Teams\\u2019 dashboard and run a sample request in staging\\\\n- PagerDuty: able to view on-call rota and acknowledge a test alert\\\\n- Datadog: able to view sample dashboards and logs\\\\n\\\\nFirst-week recommended agenda (sample):\\\\n- Day 1 morning: People Ops orientation (benefits walkthrough, payroll, policies), office tour or virtual welcome, equipment handoff.\\\\n- Day 1 afternoon: Team intro, assign buddy, first 1:1 with manager (30m), access verification walkthrough.\\\\n- Day 2: Codebase orientation (eng), product roadmap overview (product), sales shadow (go-to-market).\\\\n- Day 3: Security and compliance deep-dive (required), CI/CD demo, sample PR and deploy walkthrough.\\\\n- Day 4: Start first small onboarding task and pair with buddy.\\\\n- Day 5: Manager 1:1 + set 30/60/90 objectives.\\\\n\\\\n30/60/90 Templates (role-agnostic, editable):\\\\n- 30 days: Observe, learn internal workflows, complete mandatory trainings, deliver first small task or doc.\\\\n- 60 days: Own a non-critical feature or process, demonstrate familiarity with primary tools, participate in on-call shadowing if role requires.\\\\n- 90 days: Independently ship a medium-sized piece of work, present a retrospective on onboarding, and agree on promotion/career goals with manager.\\\\n\\\\nRole-specific starters (high level):\\\\n- Engineering: clone main repos, run local dev with `make dev`, create a test feature branch, complete the runtime onboarding lab in the Console sandbox.\\\\n- SRE / Platform: validate runbooks, join on-call shadow, perform a canary deploy in staging with telemetry checks.\\\\n- Product / PM: review 3 recent PRDs, join customer calls, author a small requirement doc and sync with design.\\\\n- Sales / CS: complete security and data-handling training, shadow enterprise onboarding call, review contract templates and SLA docs.\\\\n\\\\nHardware & equipment policy summary:\\\\n- Standard issue laptop: M1/M2 MacBook Pro (engineering preferred) or equivalent Windows device.\\\\n- Perks budget for monitors, ergonomic chair reimbursement up to $400.\\\\n- Replacement lifecycle: 36 months standard; expedited replacement available for critical failures.\\\\n- Device enrollment: All company devices must be enrolled in MDM and disk encryption enabled.\\\\n\\\\nExpense & procurement process (short):\\\\n1. Fill device/expense request at /tools/device-request.\\\\n2. Manager approval via JIRA workflow.\\\\n3. IT issues fulfillment ticket, tracks via procurement board.\\\\n4. Submit receipts to Expensify under project code REDWOOD-OPS.\\\\n\\\\nSecurity and compliance checkpoints (must be completed by end of week 1):\\\\n- Complete security awareness training.\\\\n- Confirm MFA is enabled on all accounts.\\\\n- Sign data handling acknowledgement and NDAs where applicable.\\\\n- For private deployments or customer-sensitive roles, complete additional onboarding checklist provided by Security (link in People Ops JIRA).\\\\n\\\\nInternal tools primer (what to use when):\\\\n- Slack: informal and synchronous team communication. Use #team-<name>, #all-hands, and private channels for sensitive topics.\\\\n- Confluence: single source of truth for processes, runbooks, and design docs. Use templates for PRDs and ADRs.\\\\n- GitHub: code, PR reviews, and issue tracking. Branch naming convention: team/short-desc.\\\\n- CI/CD: Buildkite for most engineering pipelines; run the `buildkite setup` task in the onboarding lab.\\\\n- PagerDuty: on-call notifications and escalation. Make sure your local mobile app notifications are enabled.\\\\n- Datadog: service dashboards, logs, synthetic checks. Dashboards live under `teams/<team-name>`.\\\\n- Okta: SSO and MFA management. Use Okta to access internal apps.\\\\n- Vault/KMS: secrets access is role-based and requires requesting a Vault token scoped to projects.\\\\n- Redwood Console (internal): production and staging routing, model deployments, and telemetry. New hires get read access to sandbox by default; production access is provisioned by manager request.\\\\n\\\\nManager responsibilities (short list):\\\\n- Own the 30/60/90 goals and provide weekly check-ins for the first 90 days.\\\\n- Assign an onboarding buddy and ensure pairing sessions.\\\\n- Verify critical access and remove blockers within SLA.\\\\n- Outline clear success metrics for the first 90 days and review them at week 2 and week 8.\\\\n\\\\nBuddy program (how it works):\\\\n- Buddy length: 6 weeks. Goals: answer day-to-day questions, demo workflows, and provide social context.\\\\n- Recommended time commitment: 2 hours/week of paired time for the first 3 weeks, then 1 hour/week.\\\\n\\\\nCommon onboarding blockers & escalation path:\\\\n- Missing GitHub access: escalate to DevOps lead and tag #onboarding-help in Slack.\\\\n- Laptop delivery delay > 7 days: People Ops to escalate to procurement; provide temporary cloud workstation.\\\\n- Console access failure: open ticket with Platform team and request temporary staging credentials.\\\\n\\\\nMeasuring onboarding success (KPIs):\\\\n- Day-1 access completion rate (target: 95%)\\\\n- Time-to-first-merge (median) (target: <= 21 days for engineers)\\\\n- New-hire satisfaction score from 30-day survey (target: >= 4.0/5)\\\\n\\\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Access request templates (copy into JIRA):\\\\n- GitHub access request: \\\\\\\"Team: <team-name> \\u2014 New hire <name> \\u2014 Repos: <list> \\u2014 Role: write/read\\\\\\\"\\\\n- Console production access request: \\\\\\\"New hire <name> \\u2014 Customer scope: <customer> \\u2014 Justification: <reason> \\u2014 Manager approval required\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nAppendix B \\u2014 Sample first ticket for a new engineering hire (copy to repo):\\\\nTitle: onboarding: hello-world endpoint\\\\nDescription: Create a small hello-world endpoint that returns service health. Steps: 1) create branch team/onboarding-hello 2) add endpoint and tests 3) open PR with 'onboarding' label 4) assign buddy for review\\\\n\\\\nContacts (owners):\\\\n- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (Maya Patel)\\\\n- IT / Procurement: it-ops@redwood.ai (Liam Chen)\\\\n- Security: security@redwood.ai (Rupa Singh)\\\\n- Platform access requests: platform-ops@redwood.ai (Andre Gomez)\\\\n\\\\nRevision history:\\\\n- 2024-11-15: Created by Maya Patel (initial playbook).\\\\n- 2025-02-10: Updated SLAs and added Console sandbox steps (reviewed by Rupa Singh).\\\\n\\\\nIf you have feedback or a correction, please use the People Ops onboarding JIRA and tag the document owners above.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: New Hire Orientation & Tooling Playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/company-handbook/04_hiring-and-onboarding/new-hire-orientation-and-tooling-guide-2024.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: company-handbook\n\nn6. grant github org membership and base repo access ( create pr template if repo requires ). \\ n7. assign mandatory trainings : security, privacy, code of conduct ( links provided in the people ops jira ). \\ n8. schedule 60 - minute orientation with people ops and 30 - minute manager check - in for day 1. \\ n9. assign onboarding buddy and create calendar invites for first - week paired sessions. \\ n10. run through initial access verification script ( see access verification below ). \\ n \\ naccess verification ( run with new hire on day 1 ) : \\ n - okta sso login successful \\ n - email access and distribution lists verified \\ n - slack signed in on desktop and mobile \\ n - github access to at least 2 rep",

document.title: New Hire Orientation & Tooling Playbook
document.content:
{
  "title": "New Hire Orientation & Tooling Playbook",
  "space": "company-handbook",
  "author": "Maya Patel",
  "owner_team": "people-ops",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-11-15",
  "last_updated": "2025-02-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Liam Chen",
    "Rupa Singh",
    "Andre Gomez"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "onboarding",
    "new-hire",
    "tools",
    "people-ops"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/company-handbook/00_overview/employee-handbook-2024",
    "/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/one-click-dev-setup"
  ],
  "content": "Overview:\\n\\nThis playbook is the canonical guide for orienting new hires at Redwood Inference. It combines the people-ops onboarding checklist, role-specific 30/60/90 templates, access provisioning procedures, an internal tools primer, and first-week agenda recommendations. Use this doc to coordinate hiring managers, IT, security, and the new hire so that day 1 is productive and secure.\\n\\nWho this is for:\\n- Hiring managers preparing a new joiner\\n- People Ops coordinators running orientation\\n- IT/Security staff provisioning accounts and devices\\n- New hires who want a single source of truth for the first 90 days\\n\\nGoals:\\n- Ensure all essential accounts and hardware are provisioned by day 1 (target SLA below).\\n- Provide a clear 30/60/90 learning and success plan for common roles.\\n- Standardize tooling orientation so engineers, product, and SREs can ship quickly and securely.\\n\\nQuick links (internal):\\n- People Ops onboarding JIRA: /jira/POPS-ONBOARD\\n- Device procurement form: /tools/device-request\\n- Okta SSO admin: https://okta.redwood.local\\n- Console sandbox: https://console-sandbox.redwood.local\\n\\nOnboarding SLAs (target):\\n| Item | SLA (business days) | Owner |\\n|---|---:|---|\\n| Okta / core SSO account enabled | 1 | People Ops / IT |\\n| GitHub org membership + repo access | 2 | Eng manager / DevOps |\\n| PagerDuty & Datadog alert access | 2 | Eng SRE |\\n| Laptop procurement (if new) | 3-7 | IT procurement |\\n| Security training assigned | 1 | Security |\\n| Full access to Redwood Console (prod sandbox role) | 3 | Platform team |\\n\\nNote: these are targets. Use expedited channel when access will block day-1 work.\\n\\nDay 0-1 Checklist (numbered steps for managers + Ops):\\n1. Confirm start date and arrival window with People Ops.\\n2. Add new hire to People Ops onboarding JIRA and attach signed offer.\\n3. Create Okta account and add to SSO groups (engineering/product/sales as appropriate).\\n4. Request laptop via Device procurement form (include preferred OS, accessories).\\n5. Add to relevant Slack channels, Mail Groups, and Confluence spaces.\\n6. Grant GitHub org membership and base repo access (create PR template if repo requires).\\n7. Assign mandatory trainings: security, privacy, code of conduct (links provided in the People Ops JIRA).\\n8. Schedule 60-minute orientation with People Ops and 30-minute manager check-in for day 1.\\n9. Assign onboarding buddy and create calendar invites for first-week paired sessions.\\n10. Run through initial access verification script (see Access Verification below).\\n\\nAccess Verification (run with new hire on day 1):\\n- Okta SSO login successful\\n- Email access and distribution lists verified\\n- Slack signed in on desktop and mobile\\n- GitHub access to at least 2 repos: onboarding and team repo\\n- Console sandbox access: able to view the \u2018Teams\u2019 dashboard and run a sample request in staging\\n- PagerDuty: able to view on-call rota and acknowledge a test alert\\n- Datadog: able to view sample dashboards and logs\\n\\nFirst-week recommended agenda (sample):\\n- Day 1 morning: People Ops orientation (benefits walkthrough, payroll, policies), office tour or virtual welcome, equipment handoff.\\n- Day 1 afternoon: Team intro, assign buddy, first 1:1 with manager (30m), access verification walkthrough.\\n- Day 2: Codebase orientation (eng), product roadmap overview (product), sales shadow (go-to-market).\\n- Day 3: Security and compliance deep-dive (required), CI/CD demo, sample PR and deploy walkthrough.\\n- Day 4: Start first small onboarding task and pair with buddy.\\n- Day 5: Manager 1:1 + set 30/60/90 objectives.\\n\\n30/60/90 Templates (role-agnostic, editable):\\n- 30 days: Observe, learn internal workflows, complete mandatory trainings, deliver first small task or doc.\\n- 60 days: Own a non-critical feature or process, demonstrate familiarity with primary tools, participate in on-call shadowing if role requires.\\n- 90 days: Independently ship a medium-sized piece of work, present a retrospective on onboarding, and agree on promotion/career goals with manager.\\n\\nRole-specific starters (high level):\\n- Engineering: clone main repos, run local dev with `make dev`, create a test feature branch, complete the runtime onboarding lab in the Console sandbox.\\n- SRE / Platform: validate runbooks, join on-call shadow, perform a canary deploy in staging with telemetry checks.\\n- Product / PM: review 3 recent PRDs, join customer calls, author a small requirement doc and sync with design.\\n- Sales / CS: complete security and data-handling training, shadow enterprise onboarding call, review contract templates and SLA docs.\\n\\nHardware & equipment policy summary:\\n- Standard issue laptop: M1/M2 MacBook Pro (engineering preferred) or equivalent Windows device.\\n- Perks budget for monitors, ergonomic chair reimbursement up to $400.\\n- Replacement lifecycle: 36 months standard; expedited replacement available for critical failures.\\n- Device enrollment: All company devices must be enrolled in MDM and disk encryption enabled.\\n\\nExpense & procurement process (short):\\n1. Fill device/expense request at /tools/device-request.\\n2. Manager approval via JIRA workflow.\\n3. IT issues fulfillment ticket, tracks via procurement board.\\n4. Submit receipts to Expensify under project code REDWOOD-OPS.\\n\\nSecurity and compliance checkpoints (must be completed by end of week 1):\\n- Complete security awareness training.\\n- Confirm MFA is enabled on all accounts.\\n- Sign data handling acknowledgement and NDAs where applicable.\\n- For private deployments or customer-sensitive roles, complete additional onboarding checklist provided by Security (link in People Ops JIRA).\\n\\nInternal tools primer (what to use when):\\n- Slack: informal and synchronous team communication. Use #team-<name>, #all-hands, and private channels for sensitive topics.\\n- Confluence: single source of truth for processes, runbooks, and design docs. Use templates for PRDs and ADRs.\\n- GitHub: code, PR reviews, and issue tracking. Branch naming convention: team/short-desc.\\n- CI/CD: Buildkite for most engineering pipelines; run the `buildkite setup` task in the onboarding lab.\\n- PagerDuty: on-call notifications and escalation. Make sure your local mobile app notifications are enabled.\\n- Datadog: service dashboards, logs, synthetic checks. Dashboards live under `teams/<team-name>`.\\n- Okta: SSO and MFA management. Use Okta to access internal apps.\\n- Vault/KMS: secrets access is role-based and requires requesting a Vault token scoped to projects.\\n- Redwood Console (internal): production and staging routing, model deployments, and telemetry. New hires get read access to sandbox by default; production access is provisioned by manager request.\\n\\nManager responsibilities (short list):\\n- Own the 30/60/90 goals and provide weekly check-ins for the first 90 days.\\n- Assign an onboarding buddy and ensure pairing sessions.\\n- Verify critical access and remove blockers within SLA.\\n- Outline clear success metrics for the first 90 days and review them at week 2 and week 8.\\n\\nBuddy program (how it works):\\n- Buddy length: 6 weeks. Goals: answer day-to-day questions, demo workflows, and provide social context.\\n- Recommended time commitment: 2 hours/week of paired time for the first 3 weeks, then 1 hour/week.\\n\\nCommon onboarding blockers & escalation path:\\n- Missing GitHub access: escalate to DevOps lead and tag #onboarding-help in Slack.\\n- Laptop delivery delay > 7 days: People Ops to escalate to procurement; provide temporary cloud workstation.\\n- Console access failure: open ticket with Platform team and request temporary staging credentials.\\n\\nMeasuring onboarding success (KPIs):\\n- Day-1 access completion rate (target: 95%)\\n- Time-to-first-merge (median) (target: <= 21 days for engineers)\\n- New-hire satisfaction score from 30-day survey (target: >= 4.0/5)\\n\\nAppendix A \u2014 Access request templates (copy into JIRA):\\n- GitHub access request: \\\"Team: <team-name> \u2014 New hire <name> \u2014 Repos: <list> \u2014 Role: write/read\\\"\\n- Console production access request: \\\"New hire <name> \u2014 Customer scope: <customer> \u2014 Justification: <reason> \u2014 Manager approval required\\\"\\n\\nAppendix B \u2014 Sample first ticket for a new engineering hire (copy to repo):\\nTitle: onboarding: hello-world endpoint\\nDescription: Create a small hello-world endpoint that returns service health. Steps: 1) create branch team/onboarding-hello 2) add endpoint and tests 3) open PR with 'onboarding' label 4) assign buddy for review\\n\\nContacts (owners):\\n- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai (Maya Patel)\\n- IT / Procurement: it-ops@redwood.ai (Liam Chen)\\n- Security: security@redwood.ai (Rupa Singh)\\n- Platform access requests: platform-ops@redwood.ai (Andre Gomez)\\n\\nRevision history:\\n- 2024-11-15: Created by Maya Patel (initial playbook).\\n- 2025-02-10: Updated SLAs and added Console sandbox steps (reviewed by Rupa Singh).\\n\\nIf you have feedback or a correction, please use the People Ops onboarding JIRA and tag the document owners above.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "content"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_426645772b534ac4a6af358830cf7982"
}

    "title": "Regional Flow Shepherd: Coordinated active-active edge failover, stream affinity & load-shedding playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-17385\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Regional Flow Shepherd: Coordinated active-active edge failover, stream affinity & load-shedding playbook\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-03-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-20\",\n  \"creator\": \"Sanjay Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marisa Chong\",\n  \"project\": \"runtime-resilience\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W12\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-04-10\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"slo\",\n    \"multi-region\",\n    \"failover\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"circuit-breaker\",\n    \"load-shedding\",\n    \"observability\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"ENG-14257\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-22418\",\n    \"ENG-14257\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.22\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Goal: Define and implement a coordinated active-active edge failover pattern that minimizes customer-visible disruptions for short-lived API calls and long-lived streaming sessions while preserving SLOs and predictable error-budget burns. This ticket captures design, implementation steps, telemetry, and the operational playbook for runbooks and rollout. Key constraints: maintain low p50/p95 latency for non-degraded traffic, bound p99 tail from cascading failovers, and provide graceful streaming degradation (partial transcript preservation / deterministic fallback).\",\n  \"technical_design\": \"High-level approach: 1) Per-request scoring + routing policy: compute a region health score (latency, error-rate, queue-depth, token-balance) and choose primary region for each request using sticky affinity tokens with TTL. 2) Two-layer circuit breakers: local-region soft-circuit (per-node, fast detection) and global-region hard-circuit (aggregated, conservative) with separate thresholds and cooldown windows. 3) Streaming handshake extension: embed ephemeral affinity token + stream-session version; on region shift, perform a short-lived proxy relay for remaining TTL to avoid breaking open streams. 4) Graceful degrade: when streaming cannot be preserved, return structured partial-result with deterministic resume token and stable fallback to a lower-throughput but more available model variant. 5) Load-shedding policy: reactive (score driven) and proactive (traffic shaping windows) modes; prefer shedding by token-class (background/low-priority customers) before dropping production-critical requests. 6) KV/Prefix cache sync: ensure KV cache pre-warm on target region during planned shift, with progressive warming using traffic mirroring. 7) Telemetry tagging: every request annotated with route_decision, origin_region, chosen_region, affinity_token, circuit_state, shed_reason (if dropped).\",\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"Phase 0: Simulate traffic in staging with synthetic high-latency/failure injections and verify scoring decisions. Phase 1: Canary active for 5% of production traffic for low-risk orgs; observe error budget burn and p99. Phase 2: Open rollout to 25% with automatic rollback triggers tied to error budget and p99 delta. Phase 3: Full rollout with documentation and Ops runbook. Rollback criteria: sustained region p99 increase > 2x baseline for 5m or error budget burn > 30% in 1h. During rollout enable 'preserve-streams' flag only for customers on Dedicated/Demo tiers until stable.\",\n  \"telemetry_and_alerting\": [\n    \"Metrics: regional_p50/p95/p99_latency, regional_error_rate, region_queue_depth, affinity_stickiness_ratio, partial_resume_success_rate\",\n    \"Derived: region_health_score (0-100), failover_count_by_region, shed_rate_by_priority_tier\",\n    \"SLOs: total API availability >= 99.95% global; regional degradations allowed if global availability preserved. Per-customer streaming availability objective: 99.9% for sticky sessions for 5m windows\",\n    \"Alerts: page on region_health_score < 40 for > 2m; page on failover_count spike > 50 in 10m; warn on shed_rate > 1% for production tier\",\n    \"Logging: structured events for routing_decision and circuit_transitions sent to central observability with sampling for full traces\"\n  ],\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Routing decisions must be reproducible in staging with the same inputs (region load, token TTL, customer priority)\",\n    \"Local soft-circuits trip and recover within expected windows without causing global circuit cascade in injected-failure scenarios\",\n    \"Active canary must not increase global error budget burn by more than 10% during a 24h test\",\n    \"Streams that are promoted during a regional shift should either be preserved via short-lived relay (>= 90% success) or return deterministic resume tokens enabling resumed continuity\",\n    \"Load-shedding must prioritize non-critical token classes and provide a clear shed_reason for metrics and billing reconciliation\",\n    \"Playbook documented and Ops team validated on rollback/runbook steps; runbook drill executed once before full release\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime-resilience/regional-flow-shepherd-design\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4921\",\n    \"https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/edge-health?orgId=1&var-region=all\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/active-active-failover.md\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-03-13 - Marisa: Initial design sketch complete. Basic telemetry events are emitted. Next: integrate streaming handshake changes and test partial-resume logic.\",\n    \"2025-03-20 - Security (Riley): KMS review required for resume tokens since they encode session resumption.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Regional Flow Shepherd: Coordinated active-active edge failover, stream affinity & load-shedding playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-17385-regional-flow-shepherd-playbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: runtime-resilience\nTeam: engineering\n\ntechnical design : high - level approach : 1 ) per - request scoring + routing policy : compute a region health score ( latency, error - rate, queue - depth, token - balance ) and choose primary region for each request using sticky affinity tokens with ttl. 2 ) two - layer circuit breakers : local - region soft - circuit ( per - node, fast detection ) and global - region hard - circuit ( aggregated, conservative ) with separate thresholds and cooldown windows. 3 ) streaming handshake extension : embed ephemeral affinity token + stream - session version ; on region shift, perform a short - lived proxy relay for remaining ttl to avoid breaking open streams. 4 ) graceful degrade : when streaming cannot be preserved, return structured partial - result with deter",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Regional Flow Shepherd: Coordinated active-active edge failover, stream affinity & load-shedding playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-17385-regional-flow-shepherd-playbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: runtime-resilience\nTeam: engineering\n\navoid breaking open streams. 4 ) graceful degrade : when streaming cannot be preserved, return structured partial - result with deterministic resume token and stable fallback to a lower - throughput but more available model variant. 5 ) load - shedding policy : reactive ( score driven ) and proactive ( traffic shaping windows ) modes ; prefer shedding by token - class ( background / low - priority customers ) before dropping production - critical requests. 6 ) kv / prefix cache sync : ensure kv cache pre - warm on target region during planned shift, with progressive warming using traffic mirroring. 7 ) telemetry tagging : every request annotated with route _ decision, origin _ region, chosen _ region, affinity _ token, circuit _ state, shed _ reason ( if dropped ).",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Regional Flow Shepherd: Coordinated active-active edge failover, stream affinity & load-shedding playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-17385-regional-flow-shepherd-playbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: runtime-resilience\nTeam: engineering\n\n# # acceptance criteria - routing decisions must be reproducible in staging with the same inputs ( region load, token ttl, customer priority ) - local soft - circuits trip and recover within expected windows without causing global circuit cascade in injected - failure scenarios - active canary must not increase global error budget burn by more than 10 % during a 24h test - streams that are promoted during a regional shift should either be preserved via short - lived relay ( > = 90 % success ) or return deterministic resume tokens enabling resumed continuity - load - shedding must prioritize non - critical token classes and provide a clear shed _ reason for metrics and billing reconciliation - playbook documented and ops team validated on rollback / runbook steps ; runbook drill executed once before full release",

{
  "key": "ENG-17385",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Regional Flow Shepherd: Coordinated active-active edge failover, stream affinity & load-shedding playbook",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2025-03-12",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-20",
  "creator": "Sanjay Patel",
  "assignee": "Marisa Chong",
  "project": "runtime-resilience",
  "cycle": "2025-W12",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2025-04-10",
  "labels": [
    "slo",
    "multi-region",
    "failover",
    "streaming",
    "circuit-breaker",
    "load-shedding",
    "observability"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "ENG-14257"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-22418",
    "ENG-14257"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "runtime-1.22",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "Goal: Define and implement a coordinated active-active edge failover pattern that minimizes customer-visible disruptions for short-lived API calls and long-lived streaming sessions while preserving SLOs and predictable error-budget burns. This ticket captures design, implementation steps, telemetry, and the operational playbook for runbooks and rollout. Key constraints: maintain low p50/p95 latency for non-degraded traffic, bound p99 tail from cascading failovers, and provide graceful streaming degradation (partial transcript preservation / deterministic fallback).",
  "technical_design": "High-level approach: 1) Per-request scoring + routing policy: compute a region health score (latency, error-rate, queue-depth, token-balance) and choose primary region for each request using sticky affinity tokens with TTL. 2) Two-layer circuit breakers: local-region soft-circuit (per-node, fast detection) and global-region hard-circuit (aggregated, conservative) with separate thresholds and cooldown windows. 3) Streaming handshake extension: embed ephemeral affinity token + stream-session version; on region shift, perform a short-lived proxy relay for remaining TTL to avoid breaking open streams. 4) Graceful degrade: when streaming cannot be preserved, return structured partial-result with deterministic resume token and stable fallback to a lower-throughput but more available model variant. 5) Load-shedding policy: reactive (score driven) and proactive (traffic shaping windows) modes; prefer shedding by token-class (background/low-priority customers) before dropping production-critical requests. 6) KV/Prefix cache sync: ensure KV cache pre-warm on target region during planned shift, with progressive warming using traffic mirroring. 7) Telemetry tagging: every request annotated with route_decision, origin_region, chosen_region, affinity_token, circuit_state, shed_reason (if dropped).",
  "rollout_plan": "Phase 0: Simulate traffic in staging with synthetic high-latency/failure injections and verify scoring decisions. Phase 1: Canary active for 5% of production traffic for low-risk orgs; observe error budget burn and p99. Phase 2: Open rollout to 25% with automatic rollback triggers tied to error budget and p99 delta. Phase 3: Full rollout with documentation and Ops runbook. Rollback criteria: sustained region p99 increase > 2x baseline for 5m or error budget burn > 30% in 1h. During rollout enable 'preserve-streams' flag only for customers on Dedicated/Demo tiers until stable.",
  "telemetry_and_alerting": [
    "Metrics: regional_p50/p95/p99_latency, regional_error_rate, region_queue_depth, affinity_stickiness_ratio, partial_resume_success_rate",
    "Derived: region_health_score (0-100), failover_count_by_region, shed_rate_by_priority_tier",
    "SLOs: total API availability >= 99.95% global; regional degradations allowed if global availability preserved. Per-customer streaming availability objective: 99.9% for sticky sessions for 5m windows",
    "Alerts: page on region_health_score < 40 for > 2m; page on failover_count spike > 50 in 10m; warn on shed_rate > 1% for production tier",
    "Logging: structured events for routing_decision and circuit_transitions sent to central observability with sampling for full traces"
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Routing decisions must be reproducible in staging with the same inputs (region load, token TTL, customer priority)",
    "Local soft-circuits trip and recover within expected windows without causing global circuit cascade in injected-failure scenarios",
    "Active canary must not increase global error budget burn by more than 10% during a 24h test",
    "Streams that are promoted during a regional shift should either be preserved via short-lived relay (>= 90% success) or return deterministic resume tokens enabling resumed continuity",
    "Load-shedding must prioritize non-critical token classes and provide a clear shed_reason for metrics and billing reconciliation",
    "Playbook documented and Ops team validated on rollback/runbook steps; runbook drill executed once before full release"
  ],
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime-resilience/regional-flow-shepherd-design",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4921",
    "https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/edge-health?orgId=1&var-region=all",
    "https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/active-active-failover.md"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2025-03-13 - Marisa: Initial design sketch complete. Leaning toward two-tier circuit breaker to avoid region-wide cascades. Need input from batching team on KV cache warm-up latency.",
    "2025-03-15 - Alex G.: Concern: preserving live streams via relay has bandwidth and cost implications. Proposal: only relay sessions tagged 'high-priority' and provide deterministic resume tokens for the rest.",
    "2025-03-17 - Product (Ana): Product asks that when we shed, we expose a fine-grained metric and explainable 'why' value in the response header for customer-side handling.",
    "2025-03-19 - Marisa: Implemented simulated region scoring and soft-circuit in staging. Basic telemetry events are emitted. Next: integrate streaming handshake changes and test partial-resume logic.",
    "2025-03-20 - Security (Riley): KMS review required for resume tokens since they encode session resumption. Marking security_review_required=true."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "technical_design",
    "rollout_plan",
    "telemetry_and_alerting",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_501d5f0ba32a4728a72d743ea5144f70"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_63dc81476f6047fdbdf584c3bcd64f77",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9402-canary-rollback-postmortem-actions-and-safety-automation.json",
    "title": "Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-9402\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-20\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-05\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marcelo Ruiz\",\n  \"project\": \"Model-lifecycle-tooling\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W08\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-12\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"canary-rollout\",\n    \"postmortem\",\n    \"auto-rollback\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"ENG-8739\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-7124\",\n    \"ENG-9021\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.19\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Summary: During a recent canary rollout of model v2.3 we observed a progressive increase in bad response rates across a small percentage of traffic and an eventual failed auto-rollback because the safety gate hysteresis allowed transient noise to be treated as stable regressions. This ticket captures the postmortem actions and tracks engineering work to harden canary safety gates, add automated sanity-runbooks, and implement a configurable rollback TTL and probe smoothing to avoid flapping.\\n\\nGoals: \\n- Collect incident learnings and formalize them into a canary safety runbook.\\n- Implement probe hysteresis and exponential backoff to reduce false positives from transient spikes.\\n- Add a rollback TTL and a circuit-breaker to prevent repeated rollbacks within short windows.\\n- Create automated canary dashboards and alert thresholds tied to traffic-weighted metrics.\\n- Add an audit log and post-deploy checklist that must pass before canary promotes beyond 5% traffic.\\n\\nScope: runtime canary controller, Redwood Console rollout UI, alerting rules in PagerDuty/Dashboards, runbook docs, and a follow-up QA pass on dedicated capacity behavior.\\n\\nSuccess criteria: \\n- New runbook published to Confluence with a clear escalation path and playbook steps.\\n- Canary controller implements smoothing and rollback TTL (configurable per-release).\\n- Observability dashboards with synthetic probe traces and traffic-weighted SLOs available in staging and production.\\n- One simulated canary test with injected faults runs cleanly (no false rollback) before rollout to customers.\\n\\nNotes: This is time-sensitive because the customer who triggered the incident is on a dedicated capacity contract and expects a write-up plus mitigations within 2 weeks.\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-20 \\u2014 Aisha Patel: Filed after incident INC-2025-112. Initial triage: regression signature was 0.8% bad_response_rate at 3% traffic increasing to 2.6% over 30 minutes. Canary controller rolled back once then failed to re-promote; logs show hysteresis window configured at 5 minutes which allowed noisy spike to be interpreted as sustained regression.\",\n    \"2025-02-21 \\u2014 Marcelo Ruiz: Reproduced locally with traffic replay. Root cause appears to be twofold: (1) probe smoothing configured as simple moving average with short window; (2) rollback policy lacks TTL so subsequent canary promotions immediately retriggered the same checks. Drafting patch for smoothing and TTL config in canary controller.\",\n    \"2025-02-24 \\u2014 SRE Review (Lindsey Wong): Recommended adding median-based probe plus percentile trimming to avoid outlier-driven signals. Also suggested a temporary alert to page on 1.5% sustained bad_response_rate over 20 minutes during canary windows.\",\n    \"2025-02-27 \\u2014 Design (Hiro Tanaka): Console UX update: expose a 'safety profile' selector (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with defaults and per-release overrides. Planned mockups linked.\",\n    \"2025-03-02 \\u2014 Marcelo Ruiz: Draft PR submitted implementing exponential smoothing (alpha configurable) and rollback_ttl_seconds with default 3600s. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821\",\n    \"2025-03-04 \\u2014 QA (Priya Desai): Ran canary simulation with injected 0.5% latency noise and 2x error spikes for 3 minutes \\u2014 no false positive rollback after smoothing enabled; TTL prevented immediate re-rollouts.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9402-canary-rollback-postmortem-actions-and-safety-automation.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Model-lifecycle-tooling\nTeam: engineering\n\n7124 - eng - 9021 customer impact : high release : runtime - 1. 19 security review required : false description : summary : during a recent canary rollout of model v2. 3 we observed a progressive increase in bad response rates across a small percentage of traffic and an eventual failed auto - rollback because the safety gate hysteresis allowed transient noise to be treated as stable regressions. this ticket captures the postmortem actions and tracks engineering work to harden canary safety gates, add automated sanity - runbooks, and implement a configurable rollback ttl and probe smoothing to avoid flapping.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9402-canary-rollback-postmortem-actions-and-safety-automation.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Model-lifecycle-tooling\nTeam: engineering\n\n- 2025 - 02 - 20 — aisha patel : filed after incident inc - 2025 - 112. initial triage : regression signature was 0. 8 % bad _ response _ rate at 3 % traffic increasing to 2. 6 % over 30 minutes. canary controller rolled back once then failed to re - promote ; logs show hysteresis window configured at 5 minutes which allowed noisy spike to be interpreted as sustained regression. - 2025 - 02 - 21 — marcelo ruiz : reproduced locally with traffic replay. root cause appears to be twofold : ( 1 ) probe smoothing configured as simple moving average with short window ; ( 2 ) rollback policy lacks ttl so subsequent canary promotions immediately retriggered the same checks.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9402-canary-rollback-postmortem-actions-and-safety-automation.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Model-lifecycle-tooling\nTeam: engineering\n\n- 2025 - 02 - 22 : agreed to implement exponential smoothing ( configurable alpha ) rather than longer simple moving average to keep responsiveness to real regressions. - 2025 - 02 - 23 : ttl for rollback set to default 1 hour ( 3600s ) with per - project override up to 24h. this prevents thrashing on releases with transient infra noise. - 2025 - 02 - 27 : add safety profiles to console ui. conservative profile uses 2x sensitivity threshold and 15 - minute hysteresis ; balanced uses current defaults ; aggressive is for fast iteration only behind manual approval. - 2025 - 03 - 01 : require a synthetic probe pass ( end - to - end )",

document.title: Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-9402",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Canary rollout postmortem: automated safety gates, probe hysteresis, and rollback TTLs",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2025-02-20",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-05",
  "creator": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Marcelo Ruiz",
  "project": "Model-lifecycle-tooling",
  "cycle": "2025-W08",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-03-12",
  "labels": [
    "canary-rollout",
    "postmortem",
    "auto-rollback",
    "observability",
    "runbook"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "ENG-8739"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-7124",
    "ENG-9021"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "runtime-1.19",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Summary: During a recent canary rollout of model v2.3 we observed a progressive increase in bad response rates across a small percentage of traffic and an eventual failed auto-rollback because the safety gate hysteresis allowed transient noise to be treated as stable regressions. This ticket captures the postmortem actions and tracks engineering work to harden canary safety gates, add automated sanity-runbooks, and implement a configurable rollback TTL and probe smoothing to avoid flapping.\n\nGoals: \n- Collect incident learnings and formalize them into a canary safety runbook.\n- Implement probe hysteresis and exponential backoff to reduce false positives from transient spikes.\n- Add a rollback TTL and a circuit-breaker to prevent repeated rollbacks within short windows.\n- Create automated canary dashboards and alert thresholds tied to traffic-weighted metrics.\n- Add an audit log and post-deploy checklist that must pass before canary promotes beyond 5% traffic.\n\nScope: runtime canary controller, Redwood Console rollout UI, alerting rules in PagerDuty/Dashboards, runbook docs, and a follow-up QA pass on dedicated capacity behavior.\n\nSuccess criteria: \n- New runbook published to Confluence with a clear escalation path and playbook steps.\n- Canary controller implements smoothing and rollback TTL (configurable per-release).\n- Observability dashboards with synthetic probe traces and traffic-weighted SLOs available in staging and production.\n- One simulated canary test with injected faults runs cleanly (no false rollback) before rollout to customers.\n\nNotes: This is time-sensitive because the customer who triggered the incident is on a dedicated capacity contract and expects a write-up plus mitigations within 2 weeks.",
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-20 \u2014 Aisha Patel: Filed after incident INC-2025-112. Initial triage: regression signature was 0.8% bad_response_rate at 3% traffic increasing to 2.6% over 30 minutes. Canary controller rolled back once then failed to re-promote; logs show hysteresis window configured at 5 minutes which allowed noisy spike to be interpreted as sustained regression.",
    "2025-02-21 \u2014 Marcelo Ruiz: Reproduced locally with traffic replay. Root cause appears to be twofold: (1) probe smoothing configured as simple moving average with short window; (2) rollback policy lacks TTL so subsequent canary promotions immediately retriggered the same checks. Drafting patch for smoothing and TTL config in canary controller.",
    "2025-02-24 \u2014 SRE Review (Lindsey Wong): Recommended adding median-based probe plus percentile trimming to avoid outlier-driven signals. Also suggested a temporary alert to page on 1.5% sustained bad_response_rate over 20 minutes during canary windows.",
    "2025-02-27 \u2014 Design (Hiro Tanaka): Console UX update: expose a 'safety profile' selector (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with defaults and per-release overrides. Planned mockups linked.",
    "2025-03-02 \u2014 Marcelo Ruiz: Draft PR submitted implementing exponential smoothing (alpha configurable) and rollback_ttl_seconds with default 3600s. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821",
    "2025-03-04 \u2014 QA (Priya Desai): Ran canary simulation with injected 0.5% latency noise and 2x error spikes for 3 minutes \u2014 no false positive rollback after smoothing enabled; TTL prevented immediate re-rollouts. Pending integration tests in dedicated capacity environment."
  ],
  "attachments": [
    "Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Canary+Safety+Runbook",
    "Incident: INC-2025-112 (internal) https://redwood.incidents/INC-2025-112",
    "GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821",
    "Dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/canary-health?orgId=1"
  ],
  "decision_log": [
    "2025-02-22: Agreed to implement exponential smoothing (configurable alpha) rather than longer simple moving average to keep responsiveness to real regressions.",
    "2025-02-23: TTL for rollback set to default 1 hour (3600s) with per-project override up to 24h. This prevents thrashing on releases with transient infra noise.",
    "2025-02-27: Add safety profiles to Console UI. Conservative profile uses 2x sensitivity threshold and 15-minute hysteresis; Balanced uses current defaults; Aggressive is for fast iteration only behind manual approval.",
    "2025-03-01: Require a synthetic probe pass (end-to-end) with traffic replay for every canary before crossing 5% traffic in production for Dedicated customers."
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Merge PR #4821 and rollout to staging cluster behind feature flag (assigned Marcelo).",
    "Add a temporary PagerDuty alert rule for sustained bad_response_rate during canary windows (assigned Lindsey).",
    "Publish Canary Safety Runbook and link checklist to Console promotion flow (assigned Aisha).",
    "Design finalize mockups and handoff to frontend for safety profile selector (assigned Hiro).",
    "Schedule dedicated capacity integration test with customer-rep traffic replay (assigned Priya)."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments",
    "decision_log",
    "next_steps"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_63dc81476f6047fdbdf584c3bcd64f77"
}
