    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Safe Apply + Rollback: E2E Test Strategy (CI/CD + Synthetic Load)\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-infra\",\n  \"author\": \"Sahana Iyer\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-06\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-01-26\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Connor O'Brien\",\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Chloe Martin\",\n    \"Noah Patel\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"ci-cd\",\n    \"e2e\",\n    \"safe-apply\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"flake-reduction\",\n    \"synthetic-load\",\n    \"release-readiness\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimization-config-versioning-design.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/optimization-config-service.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/runtime-optimization-config-apply-pipeline.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/how-tos/apply-optimization-config-with-canary.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rollback-optimization-config.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/safe-apply-rollback-reliability-plan.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/optimization-rollout-health-dashboard.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-safe-apply-gating-signals.json\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Overview\\nThis page defines the end-to-end (E2E) test strategy for the Safe Apply + Rollback mechanism for Optimization Config changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles). The focus is validating:\\n- Correctness of config versioning and scoping (tenant/model/region)\\n- Safe apply staged rollout behavior (canary + promote)\\n- Gating signal evaluation and pause/fail behavior\\n- One-click/API rollback semantics and runtime idempotency under retry and concurrency\\n- Audit log emission + RBAC enforcement\\n\\nThe strategy is designed to run in CI (PR gating + merge queues) and in pre-release staging pipelines with synthetic load and controlled failure injection.\\n\\n## Goals\\n1) Catch regressions before release trains enable the feature flag.\\n2) Provide high-signal failures (actionable diagnostics; minimal flakes).\\n3) Validate distributed semantics: partial apply, retries, race conditions (apply vs rollback), and eventual convergence across workers.\\n4) Validate gating correctness using real metrics plumbing (not mocked), including required tags: tenant, model, region, config_version.\\n5) Keep runtime reasonable for PR checks; run heavier soak/chaos tests on nightly or pre-release.\\n\\n## Non-goals (initial)\\n- Full performance benchmarking of all model families (covered in benchmark-lab and perf-canary workflows).\\n- Automatically proving quality improvements; we only validate that quantization quality gates behave as specified (pass/fail/noise handling).\\n- Comprehensive cross-subsystem transactional rollback coverage (out of scope in project definition).\\n\\n## System under test (SUT)\\nThe E2E tests treat the following as a single integrated system:\\n- Optimization Config Service (version storage, validation, diff, apply/rollback APIs)\\n- Canary Rollout Controller (progressive apply + pause/resume/fail)\\n- Serving runtime apply pipeline (fetch/cache/apply config version; idempotency; rollback)\\n- SLO gate evaluation hooks (error rate, latency; plus optional eval gates for quantization)\\n- Console backend endpoints (history + rollback action) where applicable\\n- Audit log pipeline (structured events; export compatibility)\\n- RBAC policy bundle checks for role-based actions\\n\\n## Environments\\n### 1) CI Ephemeral Environment (required for PRs)\\nPurpose: high-signal functional correctness with minimal infra cost.\\n\\nRequirements:\\n- Single region (e.g., staging-us-east-1)\\n- Minimal GPU pool (shared), supporting 1\\u20132 models used for tests\\n- Dedicated test tenant namespace: `ci-safe-apply-e2e` (unique per run via suffix)\\n- Control plane + config service + rollout controller deployed from current commit\\n- Runtime workers deployed from current commit\\n- Observability stack available (Prometheus-compatible metrics + log aggregation) with short retention\\n\\nConstraints:\\n- Must finish PR suite within 20\\u201330 minutes end-to-end.\\n\\n### 2) Pre-release Staging Environment (required for release trains)\\nPurpose: validate gating signals with realistic traffic patterns; detect race conditions under load.\\n\\nRequirements:\\n- Multi-region (at least 2 regions) to validate scoping and region isolation\\n- Larger worker pool (still staging), with at least two model deployments:\\n  - A chat/generation model (streaming enabled)\\n  - An embedding model (optional; to validate non-chat endpoints are unaffected)\\n- Gate evaluation stack identical to production (same SLO toolkit rules, same metric tag schema)\\n- Audit log sink configured to staging SIEM export (or staging equivalent) for schema validation\\n\\n### 3) Private Deployment Integration Environment (periodic)\\nPurpose: validate version pinning + rollback procedure in an operator-managed setting.\\n\\nRequirements:\\n- Spin a representative Kubernetes environment (kind/eks staging) with Redwood Private chart/installer\\n- Validate operator workflow for pinning config version and executing rollback (no Console dependency)\\n\\n## Test plan summary\\nWe split tests into three tiers.\\n\\n### Tier A: PR-blocking E2E (fast, deterministic)\\nRuns on every PR touching:\\n- config service / schema / validation\\n- runtime apply pipeline\\n- rollout controller\\n- audit logging / RBAC\\n- Console rollback APIs\\n\\nTarget runtime: 10\\u201320 minutes.\\n\\nCoverage:\\n1) Create config version \\u2192 validate schema \\u2192 ensure immutable version record\\n2) Safe apply to scoped target (tenant + model + region) with 5% canary \\u2192 promote to 100%\\n3) Gate evaluation wiring: confirm gate queries include required tags, and that gating decisions are honored\\n4) Rollback to prior known-good version \\u2192 confirm convergence across workers\\n5) Audit events are emitted with required fields for each lifecycle action\\n6) RBAC enforcement blocks unauthorized apply/rollback\\n\\n### Tier B: Nightly E2E + load + failure injection (medium)\\nRuns nightly and on demand before enablement.\\n\\nTarget runtime: 45\\u201390 minutes.\\n\\nAdds:\\n- Controlled latency regression injection to force gate failure\\n- Apply/rollback concurrency tests (race conditions)\\n- Worker restarts during apply (idempotency and eventual convergence)\\n- Longer canary windows to detect metric noise issues\\n\\n### Tier C: Pre-release soak + multi-region (heavy)\\nRuns for release trains (or weekly) and before Limited GA expansions.\\n\\nTarget runtime: 2\\u20134 hours.\\n\\nAdds:\\n- Multi-region scoping validation under sustained load\\n- Multi-tenant isolation validation (no leakage of config_version tags)\\n- Rollback under high concurrency; ensure rollback completes within target MTTR\\n\\n## Detailed E2E scenarios (what we assert)\\nBelow are the canonical scenarios, intended to map to the core user workflows.\\n\\n### Scenario 1: Versioning immutability + diff correctness\\nSteps:\\n1) Create baseline Optimization Config v1 for scope S (tenant T, model M, region R).\\n2) Create v2 with a small safe change (e.g., batching.max_batch_size increase within allowed range).\\n3) Fetch v1 and v2; assert:\\n   - Version IDs differ; v1 content unchanged\\n   - Metadata present: created_by, created_at, change_reason\\n4) Fetch diff; assert:\\n   - Diff highlights changed fields\\n   - Risk classification flags fields known to be risky (e.g., quantization_profile, cache.enabled)\\n\\nAssertions:\\n- Writes are append-only (no in-place mutation)\\n- Diff endpoint stable and deterministic\\n\\n### Scenario 2: Safe apply canary \\u2192 promote success path\\nSteps:\\n1) Apply v2 to scope S with canary=5%.\\n2) Start synthetic load against S. (See \\u201cSynthetic load spec\\u201d.)\\n3) Gate evaluation passes for required window (e.g., 5 minutes).\\n4) Promote to 100%.\\n5) Verify runtime convergence:\\n   - All workers serving S report active config_version=v2\\n   - Response headers (if enabled in test env) include active config version for traceability\\n\\nAssertions:\\n- Gate is consulted at each progression checkpoint\\n- Promotion updates the \\u201cactive pointer\\u201d for S (or equivalent) and workers converge\\n- No cross-scope bleed (other tenants/models/regions remain at v1)\\n\\n### Scenario 3: Gate failure pauses rollout (latency regression)\\nGoal: prove that bad changes do not auto-promote.\\n\\nSteps:\\n1) Create v3 that will cause measurable latency regression in staging (e.g., disable prefix cache or set overly aggressive batching timeout) OR use fault injection hook to add server-side delay for config_version=v3.\\n2) Apply v3 with canary=5%.\\n3) Generate load; validate p95 or error-rate gate triggers failure within the window.\\n4) Rollout controller should move to PAUSED or FAILED state (per design) and not proceed.\\n\\nAssertions:\\n- Rollout controller does not progress beyond canary\\n- Gate failure reason is recorded (which metric, threshold, observed value)\\n- Audit event includes gate failure context\\n\\n### Scenario 4: One-click/API rollback restores known-good version\\nSteps:\\n1) Ensure v2 is known-good and currently active at 100%.\\n2) Apply v3 to canary and force a gate failure.\\n3) Trigger rollback to v2 via API (Console path is validated separately; this is API truth).\\n4) Verify:\\n   - Active pointer returns to v2\\n   - Workers converge on v2 within bounded time\\n   - Synthetic load metrics recover (p95 back within threshold)\\n\\nAssertions:\\n- Rollback is idempotent (repeating the rollback request is safe)\\n- Rollback emits the correct audit event with request_id + previous/target version IDs\\n\\n### Scenario 5: Apply vs rollback race safety\\nGoal: validate fix for concurrent operations leaving mixed worker state.\\n\\nSteps:\\n1) Start apply v3 to 50% (paused midway via controller hook or time window).\\n2) Concurrently trigger rollback to v2.\\n3) Restart a subset of workers during the race.\\n\\nAssertions:\\n- Final system converges on v2 across all workers\\n- Controller state machine ends in a consistent terminal state\\n- No \\u201cstuck\\u201d shards remain at v3 after rollback completion\\n\\n### Scenario 6: RBAC enforcement\\nSteps:\\n1) Attempt apply/rollback with a token missing `optimization_config.rollback` (or equivalent) permission.\\n2) Attempt list/read endpoints with read-only role.\\n\\nAssertions:\\n- Unauthorized actions are rejected with clear error messages (403 + reason)\\n- Audit event is emitted for denied attempts only if policy requires (align with security guidance)\\n\\n### Scenario 7: Audit event schema compliance\\nFor each lifecycle action (create, validate, apply start, apply progression, promote, rollback), assert:\\n- Event name matches taxonomy\\n- Required fields present (at minimum): actor, actor_type, tenant, model, region, config_version, previous_config_version (where applicable), request_id, timestamp, outcome, reason\\n- Events can be exported to staging SIEM sink without schema errors\\n\\n## Synthetic load spec\\nSynthetic load is required to make gating meaningful.\\n\\n### Load generator requirements\\n- Must tag traffic to the exact scope under test (tenant/model/region)\\n- Must be able to run deterministic request mixes and concurrency\\n- Must report:\\n  - request success/failure counts\\n  - latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)\\n  - token counts (optional but recommended)\\n\\n### Request mix (default)\\n- 70% short prompts (<= 128 tokens)\\n- 25% medium prompts (256\\u2013512 tokens)\\n- 5% long prompts (>= 1024 tokens) to stress KV cache behavior\\n- Concurrency: 32 in CI; 128 in staging\\n- Streaming: enabled for 30% of generation calls\\n\\n### Duration\\n- CI: 5\\u20138 minutes per scenario (short gate window)\\n- Nightly: 15\\u201320 minutes for canary windows (noise detection)\\n- Soak: 60+ minutes sustained\\n\\n### Fault injection options\\nUse one of:\\n- Config-induced regression (preferred when deterministic)\\n- Runtime fault injection keyed by config_version (fallback) with bounded impact:\\n  - add fixed latency (e.g., +75ms) to a percentage of requests\\n  - force a controlled 5xx rate (e.g., 1\\u20132%) to validate error-rate gate\\n\\nAll fault injection must be guarded behind a test-only flag and must never be enabled in production.\\n\\n## Staging data and test tenants\\n- Each E2E run creates a unique tenant and cleans up resources.\\n- Model deployments use standardized names:\\n  - `ci-e2e-chat-model` (generation)\\n  - `ci-e2e-embed-model` (optional)\\n- Optimization configs must be created with an explicit `change_reason` and `created_by` referencing the CI actor.\\n\\nCleanup policy:\\n- CI: delete tenant and all associated config versions at end of run\\n- Staging soak: retain artifacts for 7 days for debugging (configs + controller state + audit event samples)\\n\\n## CI integration (pipelines + triggers)\\n### PR checks (required)\\nTrigger conditions:\\n- Changes to `optimization-config-service`, `rollout-controller`, `runtime-config-applier`, `rbac-policy-bundle`, `audit-log-schema`, Console rollback endpoints\\n\\nWorkflow outline:\\n1) Build + unit tests\\n2) Spin ephemeral environment (control plane + runtime)\\n3) Run Tier A E2E suite\\n4) Collect artifacts:\\n   - rollout controller state transitions\\n   - gate evaluation queries and results\\n   - runtime worker \\u201cactive config version\\u201d snapshots\\n   - audit log samples (JSON)\\n5) Teardown\\n\\nGating:\\n- E2E must pass for merge. Flaky tests cannot be \\u201callowed failures\\u201d on PR checks.\\n\\n### Nightly\\n- Run Tier B suite with load + failure injection\\n- Post summary to #eng-infra-ci and file an issue automatically on regression\\n\\n### Release train / pre-GA\\n- Run Tier C suite and require sign-off from Release Engineering + SRE\\n\\n## Flake reduction guidelines\\nE2E tests for distributed rollouts can be flaky without discipline. The following rules are mandatory.\\n\\n### 1) Prefer state-based waits over sleep\\n- Poll controller and runtime state with timeouts and clear progress logging.\\n- Use bounded exponential backoff.\\n\\n### 2) Make gate windows deterministic\\n- Use short, explicit measurement windows in CI.\\n- Ensure load generator warms up before gate evaluation begins.\\n\\n### 3) Control parallelism and resource contention\\n- Limit concurrent E2E jobs that share GPU pools.\\n- Avoid running multiple \\u201cheavy\\u201d scenarios simultaneously.\\n\\n### 4) Minimize reliance on external services\\n- Metrics backend must be local/staging-owned. Avoid cross-region dependencies in PR checks.\\n\\n### 5) Define retry policy explicitly\\n- Test-level retries are allowed only for known transient infrastructure steps (environment spin-up).\\n- Do not retry business-logic assertions (e.g., \\u201crollback succeeded\\u201d)\\u2014these should fail loudly.\\n\\n### 6) Quarantine process\\n- A failing test may be quarantined only with:\\n  - owner assigned\\n  - root cause hypothesis\\n  - expiration date (<= 14 days)\\n  - tracking ticket\\n\\n## Acceptance criteria (definition of \\u201cCI-ready\\u201d)\\nThe Safe Apply + Rollback feature is considered E2E-test-ready when:\\n- Tier A suite passes with >= 99% success rate over 20 consecutive runs\\n- Tier A completes within 30 minutes at p95\\n- Tier B nightly suite detects injected regressions reliably (>= 95% detection) and has <= 2% false positives\\n- Artifacts are sufficient to debug failures without re-running locally\\n\\n## Ownership and escalation\\n- Primary owner: CI/Build (Sahana Iyer)\\n- Runtime semantics: Serving Runtime (Noah Patel)\\n- Gate signal correctness and dashboards: SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant)\\n- Release gating: Release Engineering (Connor O'Brien)\\n\\nEscalation path:\\n- CI infrastructure failures \\u2192 #eng-infra-ci\\n- Gate metric/tagging issues \\u2192 #eng-sre\\n- Rollout controller logic/state machine \\u2192 #eng-platform\\n- Runtime convergence/idempotency \\u2192 #eng-runtime\\n\\n## Tracking\\nPrimary engineering ticket for this doc\\u2019s implementation: ENG-4830 (CI e2e tests covering validate\\u2192canary\\u2192promote\\u2192rollback with failure injection).\\n\\nChanges to this strategy must be reviewed by Release Engineering and SRE before they become PR-blocking requirements.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_e023ab3458e04da28d248b4568e6fd06\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Safe Apply + Rollback: E2E Test Strategy (CI/CD + Synthetic Load)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/safe-apply-e2e-test-strategy.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-infra\n\ncontent : # # overview this page defines the end - to - end ( e2e ) test strategy for the safe apply + rollback mechanism for optimization config changes ( batching, caching, quantization profiles ). the focus is validating : - correctness of config versioning and scoping ( tenant / model / region ) - safe apply staged rollout behavior ( canary + promote ) - gating signal evaluation and pause / fail behavior - one - click / api rollback semantics and runtime idempotency under retry and concurrency - audit log emission + rbac enforcement the strategy is designed to run in ci ( pr gating + merge queues ) and in pre - release staging pipelines with synthetic load and controlled failure injection.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Safe Apply + Rollback: E2E Test Strategy (CI/CD + Synthetic Load)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/safe-apply-e2e-test-strategy.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-infra\n\nsuite with load + failure injection - post summary to # eng - infra - ci and file an issue automatically on regression # # # release train / pre - ga - run tier c suite and require sign - off from release engineering + sre # # flake reduction guidelines e2e tests for distributed rollouts can be flaky without discipline. the following rules are mandatory. # # # 1 ) prefer state - based waits over sleep - poll controller and runtime state with timeouts and clear progress logging. - use bounded exponential backoff. # # # 2 ) make gate windows deterministic - use short, explicit measurement windows in ci. - ensure load generator warms up before gate evaluation begins.",

  "content": "## Overview
This page defines the end-to-end (E2E) test strategy for the Safe Apply + Rollback mechanism for Optimization Config changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles). The focus is validating:
- Correctness of config versioning and scoping (tenant/model/region)
- Safe apply staged rollout behavior (canary + promote)
- Gating signal evaluation and pause/fail behavior
- One-click/API rollback semantics and runtime idempotency under retry and concurrency
- Audit log emission + RBAC enforcement

The strategy is designed to run in CI (PR gating + merge queues) and in pre-release staging pipelines with synthetic load and controlled failure injection.

## Goals
1) Catch regressions before release trains enable the feature flag.
2) Provide high-signal failures (actionable diagnostics; minimal flakes).
3) Validate distributed semantics: partial apply, retries, race conditions (apply vs rollback), and eventual convergence across workers.
4) Validate gating correctness using real metrics plumbing (not mocked), including required tags: tenant, model, region, config_version.
5) Keep runtime reasonable for PR checks; run heavier soak/chaos tests on nightly or pre-release.

## Non-goals (initial)
- Full performance benchmarking of all model families (covered in benchmark-lab and perf-canary workflows).
- Automatically proving quality improvements; we only validate that quantization quality gates behave as specified (pass/fail/noise handling).
- Comprehensive cross-subsystem transactional rollback coverage (out of scope in project definition).

## System under test (SUT)
The E2E tests treat the following as a single integrated system:
- Optimization Config Service (version storage, validation, diff, apply/rollback APIs)
- Canary Rollout Controller (progressive apply + pause/resume/fail)
- Serving runtime apply pipeline (fetch/cache/apply config version; idempotency; rollback)
- SLO gate evaluation hooks (error rate, latency; plus optional eval gates for quantization)
- Console backend endpoints (history + rollback action) where applicable
- Audit log pipeline (structured events; export compatibility)
- RBAC policy bundle checks for role-based actions

## Environments
### 1) CI Ephemeral Environment (required for PRs)
Purpose: high-signal functional correctness with minimal infra cost.

Requirements:
- Single region (e.g., staging-us-east-1)
- Minimal GPU pool (shared), supporting 1–2 models used for tests
- Dedicated test tenant namespace: `ci-safe-apply-e2e` (unique per run via suffix)
- Control plane + config service + rollout controller deployed from current commit
- Runtime workers deployed from current commit
- Observability stack available (Prometheus-compatible metrics + log aggregation) with short retention

Constraints:
- Must finish PR suite within 20–30 minutes end-to-end.

### 2) Pre-release Staging Environment (required for release trains)
Purpose: validate gating signals with realistic traffic patterns; detect race conditions under load.

Requirements:
- Multi-region (at least 2 regions) to validate scoping and region isolation
- Larger worker pool (still staging), with at least two model deployments:
  - A chat/generation model (streaming enabled)
  - An embedding model (optional; to validate non-chat endpoints are unaffected)
- Gate evaluation stack identical to production (same SLO toolkit rules, same metric tag schema)
- Audit log sink configured to staging SIEM export (or staging equivalent) for schema validation

### 3) Private Deployment Integration Environment (periodic)
Purpose: validate version pinning + rollback procedure in an operator-managed setting.

Requirements:
- Spin a representative Kubernetes environment (kind/eks staging) with Redwood Private chart/installer
- Validate operator workflow for pinning config version and executing rollback (no Console dependency)

## Test plan summary
We split tests into three tiers.

### Tier A: PR-blocking E2E (fast, deterministic)
Runs on every PR touching:
- config service / schema / validation
- runtime apply pipeline
- rollout controller
- audit logging / RBAC
- Console rollback APIs

Target runtime: 10–20 minutes.

Coverage:
1) Create config version → validate schema → ensure immutable version record
2) Safe apply to scoped target (tenant + model + region) with 5% canary → promote to 100%
3) Gate evaluation wiring: confirm gate queries include required tags, and that gating decisions are honored
4) Rollback to prior known-good version → confirm convergence across workers
5) Audit events are emitted with required fields for each lifecycle action
6) RBAC enforcement blocks unauthorized apply/rollback

### Tier B: Nightly E2E + load + failure injection (medium)
Runs nightly and on demand before enablement.

Target runtime: 45–90 minutes.

Adds:
- Controlled latency regression injection to force gate failure
- Apply/rollback concurrency tests (race conditions)
- Worker restarts during apply (idempotency and eventual convergence)
- Longer canary windows to detect metric noise issues

### Tier C: Pre-release soak + multi-region (heavy)
Runs for release trains (or weekly) and before Limited GA expansions.

Target runtime: 2–4 hours.

Adds:
- Multi-region scoping validation under sustained load
- Multi-tenant isolation validation (no leakage of config_version tags)
- Rollback under high concurrency; ensure rollback completes within target MTTR

## Detailed E2E scenarios (what we assert)
Below are the canonical scenarios, intended to map to the core user workflows.

### Scenario 1: Versioning immutability + diff correctness
Steps:
1) Create baseline Optimization Config v1 for scope S (tenant T, model M, region R).
2) Create v2 with a small safe change (e.g., batching.max_batch_size increase within allowed range).
3) Fetch v1 and v2; assert:
   - Version IDs differ; v1 content unchanged
   - Metadata present: created_by, created_at, change_reason
4) Fetch diff; assert:
   - Diff highlights changed fields
   - Risk classification flags fields known to be risky (e.g., quantization_profile, cache.enabled)

Assertions:
- Writes are append-only (no in-place mutation)
- Diff endpoint stable and deterministic

### Scenario 2: Safe apply canary → promote success path
Steps:
1) Apply v2 to scope S with canary=5%.
2) Start synthetic load against S. (See “Synthetic load spec”.)
3) Gate evaluation passes for required window (e.g., 5 minutes).
4) Promote to 100%.
5) Verify runtime convergence:
   - All workers serving S report active config_version=v2
   - Response headers (if enabled in test env) include active config version for traceability

Assertions:
- Gate is consulted at each progression checkpoint
- Promotion updates the “active pointer” for S (or equivalent) and workers converge
- No cross-scope bleed (other tenants/models/regions remain at v1)

### Scenario 3: Gate failure pauses rollout (latency regression)
Goal: prove that bad changes do not auto-promote.

Steps:
1) Create v3 that will cause measurable latency regression in staging (e.g., disable prefix cache or set overly aggressive batching timeout) OR use fault injection hook to add server-side delay for config_version=v3.
2) Apply v3 with canary=5%.
3) Generate load; validate p95 or error-rate gate triggers failure within the window.
4) Rollout controller should move to PAUSED or FAILED state (per design) and not proceed.

Assertions:
- Rollout controller does not progress beyond canary
- Gate failure reason is recorded (which metric, threshold, observed value)
- Audit event includes gate failure context

### Scenario 4: One-click/API rollback restores known-good version
Steps:
1) Ensure v2 is known-good and currently active at 100%.
2) Apply v3 to canary and force a gate failure.
3) Trigger rollback to v2 via API (Console path is validated separately; this is API truth).
4) Verify:
   - Active pointer returns to v2
   - Workers converge on v2 within bounded time
   - Synthetic load metrics recover (p95 back within threshold)

Assertions:
- Rollback is idempotent (repeating the rollback request is safe)
- Rollback emits the correct audit event with request_id + previous/target version IDs

### Scenario 5: Apply vs rollback race safety
Goal: validate fix for concurrent operations leaving mixed worker state.

Steps:
1) Start apply v3 to 50% (paused midway via controller hook or time window).
2) Concurrently trigger rollback to v2.
3) Restart a subset of workers during the race.

Assertions:
- Final system converges on v2 across all workers
- Controller state machine ends in a consistent terminal state
- No “stuck” shards remain at v3 after rollback completion

### Scenario 6: RBAC enforcement
Steps:
1) Attempt apply/rollback with a token missing `optimization_config.rollback` (or equivalent) permission.
2) Attempt list/read endpoints with read-only role.

Assertions:
- Unauthorized actions are rejected with clear error messages (403 + reason)
- Audit event is emitted for denied attempts only if policy requires (align with security guidance)

### Scenario 7: Audit event schema compliance
For each lifecycle action (create, validate, apply start, apply progression, promote, rollback), assert:
- Event name matches taxonomy
- Required fields present (at minimum): actor, actor_type, tenant, model, region, config_version, previous_config_version (where applicable), request_id, timestamp, outcome, reason
- Events can be exported to staging SIEM sink without schema errors

## Synthetic load spec
Synthetic load is required to make gating meaningful.

### Load generator requirements
- Must tag traffic to the exact scope under test (tenant/model/region)
- Must be able to run deterministic request mixes and concurrency
- Must report:
  - request success/failure counts
  - latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
  - token counts (optional but recommended)

### Request mix (default)
- 70% short prompts (<= 128 tokens)
- 25% medium prompts (256–512 tokens)
- 5% long prompts (>= 1024 tokens) to stress KV cache behavior
- Concurrency: 32 in CI; 128 in staging
- Streaming: enabled for 30% of generation calls

### Duration
- CI: 5–8 minutes per scenario (short gate window)
- Nightly: 15–20 minutes for canary windows (noise detection)
- Soak: 60+ minutes sustained

### Fault injection options
Use one of:
- Config-induced regression (preferred when deterministic)
- Runtime fault injection keyed by config_version (fallback) with bounded impact:
  - add fixed latency (e.g., +75ms) to a percentage of requests
  - force a controlled 5xx rate (e.g., 1–2%) to validate error-rate gate

All fault injection must be guarded behind a test-only flag and must never be enabled in production.

## Staging data and test tenants
- Each E2E run creates a unique tenant and cleans up resources.
- Model deployments use standardized names:
  - `ci-e2e-chat-model` (generation)
  - `ci-e2e-embed-model` (optional)
- Optimization configs must be created with an explicit `change_reason` and `created_by` referencing the CI actor.

Cleanup policy:
- CI: delete tenant and all associated config versions at end of run
- Staging soak: retain artifacts for 7 days for debugging (configs + controller state + audit event samples)

## CI integration (pipelines + triggers)
### PR checks (required)
Trigger conditions:
- Changes to `optimization-config-service`, `rollout-controller`, `runtime-config-applier`, `rbac-policy-bundle`, `audit-log-schema`, Console rollback endpoints

Workflow outline:
1) Build + unit tests
2) Spin ephemeral environment (control plane + runtime)
3) Run Tier A E2E suite
4) Collect artifacts:
   - rollout controller state transitions
   - gate evaluation queries and results
   - runtime worker “active config version” snapshots
   - audit log samples (JSON)
5) Teardown

Gating:
- E2E must pass for merge. Flaky tests cannot be “allowed failures” on PR checks.

### Nightly
- Run Tier B suite with load + failure injection
- Post summary to #eng-infra-ci and file an issue automatically on regression

### Release train / pre-GA
- Run Tier C suite and require sign-off from Release Engineering + SRE

## Flake reduction guidelines
E2E tests for distributed rollouts can be flaky without discipline. The following rules are mandatory.

### 1) Prefer state-based waits over sleep
- Poll controller and runtime state with timeouts and clear progress logging.
- Use bounded exponential backoff.

### 2) Make gate windows deterministic
- Use short, explicit measurement windows in CI.
- Ensure load generator warms up before gate evaluation begins.

### 3) Control parallelism and resource contention
- Limit concurrent E2E jobs that share GPU pools.
- Avoid running multiple “heavy” scenarios simultaneously.

### 4) Minimize reliance on external services
- Metrics backend must be local/staging-owned. Avoid cross-region dependencies in PR checks.

### 5) Define retry policy explicitly
- Test-level retries are allowed only for known transient infrastructure steps (environment spin-up).
- Do not retry business-logic assertions (e.g., “rollback succeeded”)—these should fail loudly.

### 6) Quarantine process
- A failing test may be quarantined only with:
  - owner assigned
  - root cause hypothesis
  - expiration date (<= 14 days)
  - tracking ticket

## Acceptance criteria (definition of “CI-ready”)
The Safe Apply + Rollback feature is considered E2E-test-ready when:
- Tier A suite passes with >= 99% success rate over 20 consecutive runs
- Tier A completes within 30 minutes at p95
- Tier B nightly suite detects injected regressions reliably (>= 95% detection) and has <= 2% false positives
- Artifacts are sufficient to debug failures without re-running locally

## Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: CI/Build (Sahana Iyer)
- Runtime semantics: Serving Runtime (Noah Patel)
- Gate signal correctness and dashboards: SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant)
- Release gating: Release Engineering (Connor O'Brien)

Escalation path:
- CI infrastructure failures → #eng-infra-ci
- Gate metric/tagging issues → #eng-sre
- Rollout controller logic/state machine → #eng-platform
- Runtime convergence/idempotency → #eng-runtime

## Tracking
Primary engineering ticket for this doc’s implementation: ENG-4830 (CI e2e tests covering validate→canary→promote→rollback with failure injection).

Changes to this strategy must be reviewed by Release Engineering and SRE before they become PR-blocking requirements.",

arguments.title: Reviewed runtime investigation and promotion procedure
arguments.summary: For every runtime investigation, classify severity and affected route/model/region/release; preserve a redacted timestamped evidence set; compare with a known-good baseline; require reproduction or correlated production proof plus a disproving test; record mitigation and user-visible recovery; obtain named implementation-owner acceptance. High-risk runtime releases remain at or below 5% until end-to-end synthetic probe and traffic replay pass. Block promotion on sustained bad_response_rate >=1.5% for 20 minutes or other approved SLO gate. Validate an idempotent rollback, worker convergence, and p95/error recovery. Re-promotion requires complete evidence and SRE plus Release Engineering approval. Regional validation records global availability, error-budget burn, stream preservation/resume, and recovery time, with limitations stated explicitly.
arguments.outcome: Approved reusable investigation-and-promotion procedure stored on the isolated Runtime Diagnostics team branch.

Immediately escalate widespread multi-region failure, security-sensitive evidence, or an unsafe all-region rollback to SRE leadership and the relevant engineering lead.

## First-quarter goals

1. Establish a 90-day runtime-incident baseline with stable failure-mode and owner labels covering at least 90% of runtime incidents.
2. Reduce median time from incident declaration to correct owning-team engagement by 25%.
3. Reduce median MTTR by 15% for the top three recurring runtime failure classes and reduce recurrence in those classes by 20% quarter over quarter.
4. Publish validated diagnostic and rollback evidence packs for OOM/KV-cache, scheduling/queueing, kernel/model variant, release regression, and regional failover scenarios.
5. Add runtime-specific validation to high-risk release promotion and run at least one multi-region failover exercise, recording user-visible availability and recovery evidence.

The first-quarter charter is accepted only when all of the following are demonstrated with indexed evidence:

Team: Runtime Diagnostics

- Coverage and ownership: a 90-day backfill exists; at least 90% of runtime incidents have stable failure-mode and owning-team labels; the top three recurring classes have a named implementation owner and an approved diagnostic playbook.
- Incident outcomes: compared with the approved 90-day baseline, median owner-handoff time improves by at least 25%, median MTTR for the top three classes improves by at least 15%, and incident count in those classes falls by at least 20% quarter over quarter.
- Investigation quality: every promoted diagnosis includes timestamped route/model/region/release context, a known-good comparison, a reproduction or correlated production proof, a disproving test, mitigation outcome, redaction check, and named owner acceptance. No hypothesis is promoted solely from a dashboard correlation.
- Release safety: high-risk runtime changes cannot move beyond 5% production traffic without an end-to-end synthetic probe and traffic replay. A sustained bad-response rate of at least 1.5% for 20 minutes blocks promotion and initiates rollback review. The release suite must show at least 99% Tier-A success over 20 consecutive runs, complete within 30 minutes at p95, detect at least 95% of injected regressions, and hold false positives to at most 2%.
- Rollback validation: injected latency or 1-2% controlled 5xx regressions cause a 5% canary to pause or fail; the controller records the metric, threshold, and observed value; rollback is idempotent; all workers converge on the known-good version; and user-visible p95/error rate returns within the approved baseline threshold. A failed canary is not re-promoted until the diagnostic evidence package and SRE/Release Engineering approvals are recorded.
- Regional failover and availability: a two-region drill preserves at least 99.95% global API availability, keeps any active canary's incremental error-budget burn at or below 10% over 24 hours, and achieves at least 90% stream preservation or deterministic resumability. Stateless failover recovery is measured against the customer requirement of no more than five minutes; any inability to provide zero-loss telemetry/audit replication is explicitly documented rather than implied.
